title: A Chess Loop
summary: Keep the pawn on the board until the king and knight can build a bridge across the rook’s line.

nodes.question: How can the knight dislodge the back-rank rook?
nodes.explanation: After ...Kxg4, White has a knight and b7 pawn against a rook and two pawns. Nc6 attacks Rd8 while guarding b8.

nodes.question: Why not promote immediately while the knight guards b8?
nodes.explanation: A rook sacrifice on b8 would remove White’s last pawn. The stronger plan is to improve the king and knight first.

branches.title: Clear e7 and bridge the eighth rank
commentary: Begin after ...Kxg4 in the stable seven-piece source position. The earlier eight-piece pawn-and-knight loop remains context.
Nc6 attacks Rd8 and guards the promotion square b8.
Rh8 stays on the eighth rank, continuing to stop b8=Q.
Kxe7 removes the e-pawn and clears e7 for the king’s support of Nd8 and Nf7. The caption’s Kxc7 is corrected from the saved board.
h5 is the illustrated pawn move, leaving the rook’s back-rank blockade intact.
Nd8 blocks the rook’s eighth-rank view of b8. White has built a knight bridge protected by Ke7.
Rh7+ tries to chase the supporting king away instead of allowing promotion quietly.
Nf7 interposes against the check and is protected by Ke7, so the rook cannot simply capture it.
h4 is the illustrated final pawn move; Black still cannot stop the b-pawn.
b8=Q promotes. The exact queen-and-knight versus rook-and-pawn endpoint is a White win; further conversion is outside this selected line.
branches.explanation: b8=Q promotes. The exact queen-and-knight versus rook-and-pawn endpoint is a White win; further conversion is outside this selected line.

branches.title: Trade the last pawn for the rook too soon
commentary: Compare the source’s warning against immediate promotion before the king captures e7.
b8=Q loses White’s exact win by allowing a liquidation of its only pawn.
Rxb8 sacrifices the rook for the new queen.

Nxb8 recaptures, but leaves only king and knight against the two black pawns. This exact endpoint is a Black win, strengthening the source’s warning that only Black can play to win after the liquidation.

branches.title: Promote before the knight guards b8
commentary: This independent comparison promotes before Nc6 has protected b8.
b8=Q loses White’s exact winning position: the new queen can be taken without a knight recapture.
Rxb8 captures the queen. Black retains the exact win; the lesson stops before inventing a long rook conversion.

exercises.prompt: Why capture e7 instead of trading pawn for rook?
exercises.answer: Kxe7 leaves the b-pawn available and protects both Nd8 and Nf7. White can block the rook’s line without giving up its only promotion threat.

exercises.prompt: How does the knight bridge work?
exercises.answer: Nd8 blocks the eighth rank. After ...Rh7+, Nf7 blocks the checking rank while Ke7 protects the knight, leaving b8 free for promotion.

startContext: Begin after ...Kxg4 at 115 seconds in the seven-piece phase, reconstructed from stable saved images. The preceding eight-piece loop is context. The source rook is on h8 rather than captioned h1, and the king captures e7 rather than captioned c7. The selected Nd8/Nf7 bridge and premature promotion comparison are checked move by move; the unguarded-promotion comparison is independent.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.

sourceCorrections.claim: The captions name the defending rook square h1 and the king capture Kxc7.
